§7.3.2 E-Signature Tags

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

text-e-signature-tags · text marks forms

✅ Normative

A field that carries only an e-signature tag is unsigned and MUST be rendered as a blank, [blank]. A tag that prints a word — SIGN, INITIAL — MUST be rendered as that word, separately beside the field, and MUST NOT be rendered as a signature or as the field's value.

Electronic signing tools print a small coloured tab beside each field the signer must complete — "SIGN", "INITIAL", an arrow. The tab is not a signature and not part of the form; it is an instruction to a future signer, often left in the exported file.

QUALIFYING DISABLED VETERAN'S   │ QUALIFYING DISABLED VETERAN'S   │ DATE
SIGNATURE                       │ PRINTED NAME                    │
▸SIGN                           │                                 │

Requirements

  • The field MUST be rendered as unsigned: [blank], as for any blank field — see Fill-Ins§10.4.4.
  • A tag's printed word MUST be kept, verbatim, beside the field and outside the field's value. The samples below place it on its own line directly after the field.
  • A tag that prints no word adds nothing to the text.
  • A page on which the signature fields carry only tags is unsigned. [signature] MUST NOT appear for such a field — see Signatures§7.3.10.

✅ Sample — signature cells with signing tabs

Two signature blocks, each a three-cell row. A small red tab reading SIGN▸ sits under "SIGNATURE" in the first cell of each; every cell is otherwise empty.

Expected Markdown · excerpt, first block

…

  • QUALIFYING DISABLED VETERAN’S SIGNATURE: [blank] SIGN▸
  • QUALIFYING DISABLED VETERAN’S PRINTED NAME: [blank]
  • DATE: [blank]

✅ Sample — a tag beside a name line

A small red tab sits at the start of the Name**: line in the signature block, ahead of an otherwise blank ruled line. The tab prints no word, so nothing is added for it; every field in the block is blank.
